questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose this study destination because I have close family and personal connections in the Brisbane area, and because the University of Queensland offers a strong academic environment that aligns with my interests.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was generally very easy to find the information I needed. Both KU and UQ provided clear and helpful information channels. UQ has many different platforms and webpages, which took a bit of time to navigate in the beginning, but overall the information was easy to access.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I participated in O-Week, where I received a lot of practical information and support that helped me settle in quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was quite difficult to find off-campus housing, especially on a limited budget. In Brisbane, most rentals require you to attend an in-person inspection before you can be considered, which makes the process challenging for international students searching from abroad.
My recommendation is to arrange temporary accommodation first and then attend inspections in person, or to consider share-house options, as these often do not require formal inspections. If you have a larger budget, student housing through, for instance, Student One can be a very straightforward option, though typically more expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Rental prices can be higher than expected, and suburbs vary a lot in terms of vibe, transport options and distance to UQ. Having some temporary accommodation at the start, or at least researching potential areas in advance, makes it much easier to compare neighbourhoods and find something that fits your budget and preferences.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at UQ was straightforward. I had to apply to UQ quite early, and course enrolment opened a couple of months before arrival. About a month before the semester started, I was able to select my timetable. Overall, the steps were clearly communicated and easy to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was plenty of help available. UQ provided lots of guides and step-by-step instructions through their online portals, and it was easy to contact staff if I had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I was able to register for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My main advice is to make full use of the UQ portals, where all the guides and step-by-step instructions for registration are available. They explain the process very clearly and make enrolment much easier.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course structure was a bit different from what I am used to, as a larger share of the assessment consisted of presentations, weekly quizzes and continuous assignments. Overall, however, I found the courses to be slightly easier than at my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The overall teaching style was quite similar to UCPH, with a structure based on lectures and tutorials. The format felt familiar and easy to adapt to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ECON7200 Economics of Financial Markets, ECON7333 Big Data and Machine Learning, ECON7460 Health Economics, ECON7760 Economics of Climate Change

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend ECON7333 Big Data and Machine Learning, as it uses R throughout the course, and I was very happy to be introduced to practical coding and machine-learning tools in a structured way.

I would also recommend ECON7200 Economics of Financial Markets, which covers concepts introduced during the bachelor’s programme at UCPH and builds on them in a very applied and engaging way.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The main unexpected cost was the visa. It was very expensive, and since I also needed an extension to stay over Christmas, the additional fee made it even more costly than I had anticipated.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport was much cheaper than I expected, it costs only around AUD 0.50 per fare, regardless of distance within Queensland. Groceries were roughly in the same price range as in Denmark, although some items were noticeably more expensive and others cheaper. Eating out was generally a bit cheaper than in Denmark, and coffee was significantly cheaper, often around half the price of a to-go coffee in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of cultural, athletic and social activities available. UQ offers a wide range of student clubs, including surfing, climbing, hiking, diving and volleyball, as well as many non-sport clubs for students looking for social or cultural activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would especially recommend joining the UQ Mountain Club. I was very happy with it, they offered rock climbing twice a week and organised several hiking trips. You don’t need any prior climbing experience to join, which makes it a great way to try something new, meet people and explore Queensland.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend prioritising the inland mountains — they are absolutely stunning and often overlooked by visiting students. Of course, exploring the beaches on the Sunshine Coast and Gold Coast is also essential. I also travelled to New Zealand and was completely blown away. There are plenty of great destinations with relatively cheap fares within Australia as well, such as Cairns, the Whitsundays and the Blue Mountains.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. UQ has a highly international and student-focused environment, which made adjusting to the local culture straightforward.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: A great tip is to join non-academic clubs or student groups. It’s one of the easiest ways to meet local students and build a social network outside the classroom.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t encounter any major cultural differences that were challenging. Australians and Danes are quite similar in terms of communication style and everyday culture, so the adjustment felt very smooth.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the early-morning culture and the generally high level of outdoor activity. People are very active and spend a lot of time outside, which creates a really positive atmosphere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join non-academic clubs: it’s one of the best ways to meet people and become part of the social environment.
Start your housing search early: the rental market moves quickly, and being prepared makes the whole process easier.
Embrace the outdoor culture: Australians are very active, and taking part in the outdoor lifestyle really enhances the exchange experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
t’s useful to know that UQ has many different online platforms, which can feel overwhelming at first. But once you get used to them, everything becomes very easy to navigate. 
UQ has an enormous number of clubs, so going to Market Day in the first week is a great way to discover communities and activities you wouldn’t have expected

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was exploring Australia’s nature, from the mountains to the beaches, and experiencing a completely different outdoor culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was the planning beforehand. Even though the information channels were very good and made the process manageable, there was still a constant stream of practical things to organise before arriving.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
